entries.description: The television series that follows a 1958 Manhattan housewife who discovers a talent for stand-up comedy after her marriage collapses, built around…
entries.text: The television series that follows a 1958 Manhattan housewife who discovers a talent for stand-up comedy after her marriage collapses, built around extended single-take "oner" scenes that follow characters through overlapping vignettes across multiple settings without a cut, first commissioned by Amazon in the United States and first broadcast March 17, 2017, created by Amy Sherman-Palladino. One such sequence runs a reported twelve script pages of continuous camera movement, from a Catskills bunkhouse through an open Jeep ride to an airplane hangar, treating the single unbroken shot as a period-comedy set piece in its own right rather than a technical showpiece alone.

entries.name: The Leftovers
entries.author: Damon Lindelof and Tom Perrotta
entries.awards: Critics' Choice Television Award for Most Exciting New Series, 2014; Critics' Choice Television Award for Best Actress in a Drama Series (Carrie Coon), 2016; Television Critics Association Award for Individual Achievement in Drama, 2017.
entries.description: The television series that follows the families left behind after two percent of the world's population vanishes without explanation, first…
entries.text: The television series that follows the families left behind after two percent of the world's population vanishes without explanation, first commissioned by HBO in the United States and first broadcast June 29, 2014, co-created by Damon Lindelof with novelist Tom Perrotta from Perrotta's own book. The show relocated its entire setting and much of its supporting cast between its first and second seasons, then gave its final season a different opening title sequence for nearly every episode, tailored to that episode's own theme rather than reused week to week — two structural resets inside a single three-season run.

entries.name: Justified
entries.author: Graham Yost
entries.awards: Peabody Award, 2010; Primetime Emmy Award, Outstanding Supporting Actress in a Drama Series (Margo Martindale, as Mags Bennett), 2011; Primetime Emmy Award, Outstanding Guest Actor in a Drama Series (Jeremy Davies, as Dickie Bennett), 2012.
entries.description: The television series that follows a US Marshal returned to his Kentucky home county to police the criminal world he grew up next to, developed by…
entries.text: The television series that follows a US Marshal returned to his Kentucky home county to police the criminal world he grew up next to, developed by Graham Yost from Elmore Leonard's short story "Fire in the Hole" and Leonard's other Raylan Givens fiction, first commissioned by FX in the United States and first broadcast March 16, 2010. Boyd Crowder, the lead's chief antagonist for the rest of the series, was written to die in the pilot until test-audience response to Walton Goggins' performance got the character rewritten as a series regular starting in season two — a mid-run structural pivot around a single supporting role.

entries.name: Ted Lasso
entries.author: Jason Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt, and Joe Kelly
entries.awards: Primetime Emmy Award, Outstanding Comedy Series, 2021 and 2022; acting Emmys across its first two seasons for Sudeikis, Brett Goldstein, and Hannah Waddingham; Sam Richardson won a Guest Actor Emmy in its third season.
entries.description: The television series that follows an American college football coach hired, against all football sense, to manage an English Premier League club,…
entries.text: The television series that follows an American college football coach hired, against all football sense, to manage an English Premier League club, first commissioned by Apple TV+ in the United States and first broadcast August 14, 2020, created by Jason Sudeikis, Bill Lawrence, Brendan Hunt, and Joe Kelly. Its second season was expanded mid-production from ten episodes to twelve, with the two added episodes built to slot into the season's existing continuity without disturbing the episodes already written and shot around them — an unusually late structural expansion for a serialized comedy.

entries.name: Gilmore Girls
entries.author: Amy Sherman-Palladino
entries.awards: Primetime Emmy Award, Outstanding Makeup for a Series, 2004, for the episode "The Festival of Living Art" — the show's only Emmy win in its seven-season run.
entries.description: The television series that follows a single mother and her teenage daughter running a Connecticut inn town's social orbit, written in a rapid-fire,…
entries.text: The television series that follows a single mother and her teenage daughter running a Connecticut inn town's social orbit, written in a rapid-fire, pop-culture-dense dialogue style that ran scripts to roughly 80 pages per hour-long episode against a typical 55-to-60-page hour-drama script, first commissioned by The WB in the United States and first broadcast October 5, 2000, created by Amy Sherman-Palladino. The show's sole Emmy came not for that dialogue but for an episode built around cast members made up to resemble famous paintings — a one-off visual stunt entirely outside the series' usual register winning the recognition its everyday craft never did.

entries.name: The Americans
entries.author: Joe Weisberg
entries.awards: Primetime Emmy Award, Outstanding Lead Actor in a Drama Series (Matthew Rhys), 2018; Primetime Emmy Award, Outstanding Writing for a Drama Series (Joe Weisberg and Joel Fields, for the series finale), 2018; Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Drama, 2018; two Peabody Awards, a rare achievement for a single drama series.
entries.description: The television series that follows two KGB officers posing as an ordinary American married couple outside Washington during the Cold War, first…
entries.text: The television series that follows two KGB officers posing as an ordinary American married couple outside Washington during the Cold War, first commissioned by FX in the United States and first broadcast January 30, 2013, created by Joe Weisberg, a former CIA officer. Weisberg has described the show as fundamentally "about a marriage," using the couple's espionage tradecraft — the aliases, the compartmentalized secrets, the operational trust — as a sustained structural metaphor for an ordinary domestic relationship under strain.

entries.name: Wheel of Fortune
entries.author: Merv Griffin
entries.awards: Daytime Emmy Award for Outstanding Game Show, 2011; Pat Sajak won three Daytime Emmys for Outstanding Game Show Host, 1993, 1997, and 1998.
entries.description: The television series that pairs a wheel of dollar values with a word-guessing puzzle, contestants spinning to earn a value before guessing a…
entries.text: The television series that pairs a wheel of dollar values with a word-guessing puzzle, contestants spinning to earn a value before guessing a consonant and buying vowels once enough of the puzzle is exposed, first commissioned by NBC in the United States and first broadcast January 6, 1975, created by Merv Griffin. Its syndicated evening version, launched in 1983 alongside co-hosts Pat Sajak and Vanna White, outlasted and eventually eclipsed the original daytime network run it was spun off from.

entries.name: Jeopardy!
entries.author: Merv Griffin
entries.awards: 45 Daytime Emmy Awards altogether, including a record 19 wins in the Outstanding Game/Audience Participation Show category.
entries.description: The television series that reverses the standard quiz-show mechanic, presenting contestants with an answer to which they must supply the matching…
entries.text: The television series that reverses the standard quiz-show mechanic, presenting contestants with an answer to which they must supply the matching question, first commissioned by NBC in the United States and first broadcast March 30, 1964, created by Merv Griffin. Griffin originally required contestants to phrase their responses in strict grammatical question form, then relaxed the rule once he found that correcting phrasing mid-game slowed play down — a format constraint softened for pacing rather than for fairness.

entries.name: The Dating Game
entries.author: Chuck Barris
entries.awards: none — the original 1965 ABC run drew no major industry award nominations despite decades of syndicated revivals and heavy cultural citation as the format ancestor of nearly every blind-date dating show that followed it.
entries.description: The television series that has a contestant question three unseen potential dates from behind a partition, choosing a match on the strength of their…
entries.text: The television series that has a contestant question three unseen potential dates from behind a partition, choosing a match on the strength of their answers alone, first commissioned by ABC in the United States and first broadcast December 20, 1965, created by Chuck Barris. Certain question categories — name, age, occupation, income — were ruled off-limits by format design, forcing every question toward personality and wit instead of the biographical facts a viewer might expect to matter most in choosing a date.

entries.name: The Gong Show
entries.author: Chuck Barris
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry award nominations in its original 1976 run, its cultural footprint built entirely on notoriety and imitation rather than institutional recognition.
entries.description: The television series that lets three celebrity judges strike a gong to cut short any amateur talent act they dislike, first commissioned by NBC in…
entries.text: The television series that lets three celebrity judges strike a gong to cut short any amateur talent act they dislike, first commissioned by NBC in the United States and first broadcast June 14, 1976, created and hosted by Chuck Barris. Acts that survived a judge-set minimum duration without being gonged received scores of zero to ten from each of the three judges, turning the threat of interruption itself — not just the eventual score — into the format's central source of tension.

entries.name: Survivor (US)
entries.author: Charlie Parsons, developed for CBS by Mark Burnett
entries.awards: Emmy, Outstanding Sound Mixing, 2001; Emmy, Outstanding Special Class Program, 2002; Jeff Probst won Outstanding Host for a Reality or Reality-Competition Program four consecutive times, 2008 through 2011; the series itself has never won Outstanding Reality-Competition Program despite being one of the category's most-nominated shows since its 2003 introduction.
entries.description: The television series that strands contestants in a remote location to compete in physical and social challenges, voting one participant out at a…
entries.text: The television series that strands contestants in a remote location to compete in physical and social challenges, voting one participant out at a "tribal council" each episode until a jury of the already-eliminated decides the winner, first commissioned by CBS in the United States and first broadcast May 31, 2000, adapted by Mark Burnett from Charlie Parsons' 1997 Swedish format Expedition Robinson. Its jury-of-the-eliminated final vote — rather than a judge's decision or a studio audience — made the show's contestants themselves the format's ultimate arbiters of who deserved to win.

entries.name: The Apprentice (US)
entries.author: Mark Burnett
entries.awards: none — eight Emmy nominations across its first three seasons, including Outstanding Reality-Competition Program in both 2004 and 2005 at the show's commercial peak, converted into zero wins, a shutout its own credited producer referenced publicly for years afterward.
entries.description: The television series that divides contestants into competing business teams for weekly tasks, eliminating at least one candidate per episode in a…
entries.text: The television series that divides contestants into competing business teams for weekly tasks, eliminating at least one candidate per episode in a boardroom interrogation before a company executive, first commissioned by NBC in the United States and first broadcast January 8, 2004, created by Mark Burnett. It was the breakout ratings hit of the 2003–2004 American television season, a reception its Emmy nominations reflected without ever converting into a win in the show's flagship reality-competition category.

entries.name: Pop Idol
entries.author: Simon Fuller
entries.awards: none — Pop Idol itself drew no major British television award wins in its two-series run, its significance resting on format export rather than domestic industry recognition; the franchise it launched went on to more than fifty international versions in over 110 countries.
entries.description: The television series that narrows singing contestants through a panel-judged audition process before handing the final decision to viewer telephone…
entries.text: The television series that narrows singing contestants through a panel-judged audition process before handing the final decision to viewer telephone voting, first commissioned by ITV in the United Kingdom and first broadcast November 3, 2001, created by Simon Fuller. Once contestants passed the judges' final cut at London's Criterion Theatre, the panel lost all further say in the outcome — the rest of the competition ran entirely on audience votes, a hard structural handoff from expert judgment to public choice built into the format from its first series.

entries.name: American Idol
entries.author: Simon Fuller, adapted from Pop Idol
entries.awards: none in the Emmy's Outstanding Reality-Competition Program category despite nine nominations across its run; the Television Academy later gave the show a Governors Award, an honorary recognition made outside the competitive categories rather than a win within one.
entries.description: The television series that adapts the Pop Idol singing-competition format for American broadcast, narrowing contestants through city auditions and…
entries.text: The television series that adapts the Pop Idol singing-competition format for American broadcast, narrowing contestants through city auditions and Hollywood callbacks before handing weekly eliminations to public phone, text, and online voting, first commissioned by Fox in the United States and first broadcast June 11, 2002. For eight consecutive seasons it was the highest-rated program on American television, a ratings dominance the Emmys never once translated into a win in the genre's own marquee competitive category.

entries.name: Britain's Got Talent
entries.author: Simon Cowell
entries.awards: British Academy Television Award for Best Entertainment Programme, 2018 and 2019; Royal Television Society Programme Award, 2008.
entries.description: The television series that opens its talent-competition format to any act at all — singers, dancers, comedians, novelty performers — judged first by…
entries.text: The television series that opens its talent-competition format to any act at all — singers, dancers, comedians, novelty performers — judged first by a panel and then by public vote, first commissioned by ITV in the United Kingdom and first broadcast June 9, 2007, created by Simon Cowell. Despite its name, the American sibling format America's Got Talent actually completed its first full broadcast season a year earlier, in June 2006; the British version is still treated as the franchise's true origin because its own pilot had already been filmed months before American production began.

entries.name: MasterChef (UK original)
entries.author: Franc Roddam
entries.awards: recognized by Guinness World Records in 2017 as the world's most successful cookery television format, measured by the number of countries producing a local version.
entries.description: The television series that puts amateur home cooks through escalating culinary challenges judged by professional chefs and critics, first…
entries.text: The television series that puts amateur home cooks through escalating culinary challenges judged by professional chefs and critics, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast July 2, 1990, created by Franc Roddam. Its 1990s original run ended in 2001 and the format lay dormant for several years before a 2005 BBC relaunch rebuilt it into the internationally licensed competition-cooking template that dozens of other countries' versions, including the American MasterChef, now follow.

entries.name: Undercover Boss (UK original)
entries.author: Stephen Lambert
entries.awards: Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Reality Program, 2012 and 2013, awarded to the American licensed version rather than this original British format.
entries.description: The television series that disguises a company's own senior executive as an entry-level worker inside their own organization for one to two weeks,…
entries.text: The television series that disguises a company's own senior executive as an entry-level worker inside their own organization for one to two weeks, moving through a different role and often a different location each day before revealing their identity to reward or correct what they found, first commissioned by Channel 4 in the United Kingdom and first broadcast June 15, 2009, created by Stephen Lambert. The format's American license went on to win the reality-program Emmy this British original itself was never nominated for, an award-history split between an original format and its most decorated remake that recurs across several titles in this collection.

entries.name: So You Think You Can Dance
entries.author: Simon Fuller and Nigel Lythgoe
entries.awards: multiple Primetime Emmy Award nominations for Outstanding Choreography across its run, with individual choreographer wins in the category rather than a program-wide series win.
entries.description: The television series that puts trained dancers through open auditions, callback rounds, and live performance shows spanning multiple dance styles…
entries.text: The television series that puts trained dancers through open auditions, callback rounds, and live performance shows spanning multiple dance styles in a single season, first commissioned by Fox in the United States and first broadcast July 20, 2005, created by Simon Fuller and Nigel Lythgoe. Because contestants are judged across genres they may never have trained in — a ballroom dancer performing hip-hop one week, a hip-hop dancer performing contemporary the next — the format built genre-versatility itself into the competition's central test, distinct from the single-genre premise of most television dance competitions before it.

entries.name: Pointless
entries.author: Tom Blakeson, Simon Craig, David Flynn, Nick Mather, Richard Osman, and Shaun Parry
entries.awards: TV Choice Award, 2012; TRIC Award, 2015.
entries.description: The television series that scores contestant pairs not on being right but on being obscure, rewarding correct answers given by the fewest survey…
entries.text: The television series that scores contestant pairs not on being right but on being obscure, rewarding correct answers given by the fewest survey respondents and awarding a perfect score, "pointless," to a correct answer no survey respondent gave at all, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast August 24, 2009, devised by a team including future co-host Richard Osman. Its scoring inverts the usual quiz-show premise entirely — contestants are punished, not rewarded, for giving the answer most people would give first, making obscure correct knowledge more valuable than popular correct knowledge.

entries.name: Wipeout (US)
entries.author: Matt Kunitz and Scott Larsen
entries.awards: Kids' Choice Award for Favorite TV Show, 2012, ending American Idol's run of consecutive wins in that category since its own premiere.
entries.description: The television series that runs amateur contestants through an oversized obstacle course built largely to make them fall into water, narrowing a…
entries.text: The television series that runs amateur contestants through an oversized obstacle course built largely to make them fall into water, narrowing a field of twenty-four across three rounds to a handful of finalists for a nighttime "Wipeout Zone" timed course, first commissioned by ABC in the United States and first broadcast June 24, 2008, created by Matt Kunitz and Scott Larsen. Kunitz described the format as "ninety percent Fear Factor-inspired, ten percent Japanese game show," an acknowledged debt to shows like Takeshi's Castle and SASUKE that led Tokyo Broadcasting System to file a copyright suit against the production, later settled in 2011.

entries.name: Top Gear
entries.author: Jeremy Clarkson and Andy Wilman
entries.awards: International Emmy Award, Non-Scripted Entertainment, 2005; National Television Award for Most Popular Factual Programme, 2006, 2007, 2008, and 2011.
entries.description: The television series that rebuilt a long-running car-review magazine programme into a studio-audience format built around timed test-track laps,…
entries.text: The television series that rebuilt a long-running car-review magazine programme into a studio-audience format built around timed test-track laps, celebrity interviews, and elaborate cross-country challenge films, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast under this format October 20, 2002, reconceived by Jeremy Clarkson and Andy Wilman from the original 1977 magazine-format Top Gear. By the end of 2014 it was broadcast in 214 territories, a reach that made it, by the BBC's own description, the most widely distributed factual television programme in the world.

entries.name: Antiques Roadshow
entries.author: Bruce Parker and Robin Drake
entries.awards: none — despite running continuously since 1979 and becoming one of British television's most recognizable factual formats, it has drawn no major BAFTA or industry-award recognition in its own right; its longevity rests on audience loyalty rather than institutional award attention.
entries.description: The television series that sends antiques experts to a different regional venue each week to appraise items members of the public bring in, first…
entries.text: The television series that sends antiques experts to a different regional venue each week to appraise items members of the public bring in, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast on BBC1 February 18, 1979, set up by Bruce Parker with Robin Drake and built on a 1977 documentary pilot filmed in Hereford. Roughly fifty items are filmed on a typical shoot day but only about twenty make the final broadcast, meaning most of what happens on location — including most of the appraisals experts actually give — the audience never sees.

entries.name: University Challenge
entries.author: adapted for British television by Granada Television's Cecil Bernstein from the American format College Bowl
entries.awards: ranked 34th in the British Film Institute's 2000 list of the 100 Greatest British Television Programmes — a critical-canon citation rather than a competitive broadcasting award, since the format itself has drawn no BAFTA or similar industry win in its own right.
entries.description: The television series that pits teams of four university students against each other in a knockout tournament of individually answered starter…
entries.text: The television series that pits teams of four university students against each other in a knockout tournament of individually answered starter questions and team-conferred bonus questions, first commissioned by ITV in the United Kingdom and first broadcast September 21, 1962, adapted by Granada Television's Cecil Bernstein after he saw the American format College Bowl. Its visual presentation places the two competing teams one above the other on a split screen during starter questions, a staging choice built directly into the format rather than an incidental production flourish.

entries.name: Mastermind
entries.author: Bill Wright
entries.awards: none — beyond its own famously modest prize, a cut-glass engraved bowl for the series winner, the format has drawn no major BAFTA or industry-award recognition despite running on the BBC in some form for over five decades.
entries.description: The television series that questions a single contestant at a time first on a specialist subject of their own choosing and then on general…
entries.text: The television series that questions a single contestant at a time first on a specialist subject of their own choosing and then on general knowledge, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast September 11, 1972, created by Bill Wright, who said the format's interrogation-style black chair drew on his own experience being questioned by the Gestapo during the Second World War. Passes are tracked separately from wrong answers for tie-break purposes, a scoring distinction that rewards silence over a guess whenever a contestant is unsure.

entries.name: QI
entries.author: John Lloyd
entries.awards: Stephen Fry won a BAFTA Television Award for Best Comedy Performance in 2004 for hosting the series; the format itself drew multiple further BAFTA nominations without matching that individual win.
entries.description: The television series that awards panelists points for interesting answers regardless of accuracy and docks points for answers that are wrong in an…
entries.text: The television series that awards panelists points for interesting answers regardless of accuracy and docks points for answers that are wrong in an unforgivably obvious way, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast on BBC Four September 11, 2003, created by John Lloyd. Its scoring system is deliberately built to reward tangents and wit over correctness, inverting the usual quiz-show incentive and turning "interesting" into a scored category in its own right alongside "right."

entries.name: Would I Lie to You?
entries.author: Zeppotron, for the BBC
entries.awards: none in the BAFTA Comedy Entertainment Programme category despite nominations across more than a decade, and repeated British Comedy Award nominations over the same years — recognition that never converted into a win in either ceremony.
entries.description: The television series that has two teams try to tell whether a panelist's outlandish personal story is true or an invented lie, awarding a point to…
entries.text: The television series that has two teams try to tell whether a panelist's outlandish personal story is true or an invented lie, awarding a point to whichever side guesses correctly, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast June 16, 2007, produced by Zeppotron. Because episodes are edited down to fit a fixed broadcast slot, some scoring exchanges from the filmed session don't survive the cut — the production has had to re-record the presenter's spoken scoreboard since its sixth series so the numbers match what viewers actually see rather than what was filmed.

entries.name: 8 Out of 10 Cats
entries.author: Zeppotron, for Channel 4
entries.awards: none — despite a sixteen-year run across three UK channels and a successful crossover spin-off with Countdown, the format itself has drawn no major industry-award recognition.
entries.description: The television series that has two celebrity-captained teams answer questions drawn from opinion-poll survey statistics for comic rather than…
entries.text: The television series that has two celebrity-captained teams answer questions drawn from opinion-poll survey statistics for comic rather than factual effect, first commissioned by Channel 4 in the United Kingdom and first broadcast June 3, 2005, produced by Zeppotron. Its own scoring frequently doesn't add up on screen, because episodes are cut for time from longer filmed sessions — a discrepancy the production eventually addressed not by fixing the arithmetic but by releasing an uncut companion series, 8 Out of 10 Cats Uncut, that preserves the full gameplay elsewhere.

entries.name: RuPaul's Drag Race
entries.author: World of Wonder (Tom Campbell, with Randy Barbato and Fenton Bailey)
entries.awards: Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Reality-Competition Program, four consecutive wins, 2018 through 2021; RuPaul won the Emmy for Outstanding Host for a Reality or Competition Program eight consecutive times, 2016 through 2023.
entries.description: The television series that judges drag performers across weekly themed challenges and runway presentations, sending the bottom two into a "Lip Sync…
entries.text: The television series that judges drag performers across weekly themed challenges and runway presentations, sending the bottom two into a "Lip Sync for Your Life" elimination battle each episode, first commissioned by Logo TV in the United States and first broadcast February 2, 2009, developed by Tom Campbell with World of Wonder's Randy Barbato and Fenton Bailey. Its elimination mechanic hands the final say to a live performance contest between the two lowest-ranked contestants rather than to the judges' panel alone, making physical performance under pressure the format's last word on every episode's outcome.

entries.name: Cutthroat Kitchen
entries.author: Michael Davies
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry-award recognition across its five-season Food Network run, distinguishing it from its channel stablemate Chopped, which won two James Beard Awards in the same period.
entries.description: The television series that gives competing chefs $25,000 in prop money to bid against each other for the right to sabotage an opponent's cooking…
entries.text: The television series that gives competing chefs $25,000 in prop money to bid against each other for the right to sabotage an opponent's cooking station mid-competition, first commissioned by Food Network in the United States and first broadcast August 11, 2013, created by Michael Davies. Whatever a chef doesn't spend sabotaging rivals becomes part of their own potential winnings, turning restraint itself into a competing strategy against the format's core temptation to spend everything undermining the competition.

entries.name: Chopped
entries.author: Michael Krupat, Dave Noll, and Linda Lea
entries.awards: two James Beard Awards, 2012, for Best Show in the In-Studio or Fixed Location category and for Media Personality or Host; inducted into the Culinary Hall of Fame, 2012.
entries.description: The television series that gives four competing chefs a mandatory mystery-basket ingredient combination to build into a dish each of three rounds,…
entries.text: The television series that gives four competing chefs a mandatory mystery-basket ingredient combination to build into a dish each of three rounds, eliminating one chef per round on presentation, taste, and creativity, first commissioned by Food Network in the United States and first broadcast January 13, 2009, created by Michael Krupat, Dave Noll, and Linda Lea. Its mystery-basket constraint forces contestants toward combinations no chef would choose voluntarily, making the format's central skill improvisation under an ingredient list designed to be awkward rather than technique on ingredients of the chef's own choosing.

entries.name: The Chase
entries.author: Danny Carvalho, Pete Faherty, Chris Gepp, Elliot Johnson, Matt Pritchard, and Amanda Wilson
entries.awards: National Television Award for Best Daytime Programme or Best Quiz Show, 2016, 2017, 2019, and 2024; BAFTA Television Award for Best Daytime Programme, 2022; TRIC Award for Best Game Show, 2022 and 2023.
entries.description: The television series that has contestants bank a cash total individually before facing a professional quiz expert, the "Chaser," in a head-to-head…
entries.text: The television series that has contestants bank a cash total individually before facing a professional quiz expert, the "Chaser," in a head-to-head chase across a game board for the right to keep their winnings, first commissioned by ITV in the United Kingdom and first broadcast June 29, 2009. In its head-to-head round, an unanswered question against a locked-in opponent forces a five-second response deadline, building genuine time pressure into a format that otherwise gives contestants no clock at all during their own individual bank-building round.

entries.name: Taskmaster
entries.author: Alex Horne
entries.awards: BAFTA Television Award for Comedy Entertainment Programme, 2020; nominated in the same category in 2018.
entries.description: The television series that sets five comedians a season of bizarre, deliberately underspecified physical and creative tasks, filmed months in…
entries.text: The television series that sets five comedians a season of bizarre, deliberately underspecified physical and creative tasks, filmed months in advance and scored on tape in front of a studio audience by the host awarding points, first commissioned by the channel Dave in the United Kingdom and first broadcast July 28, 2015, created by Alex Horne. Separating task performance from task judging by months lets contestants' filmed choices be scored with the full benefit — and full risk — of hindsight neither they nor the studio audience had at the moment those choices were actually made.

entries.name: Never Mind the Buzzcocks
entries.author: Talkback, for the BBC
entries.awards: none — despite a nearly three-decade run across the BBC and a later Sky Max revival, the format itself has drawn no major industry-award recognition.
entries.description: The television series that pits two celebrity-captained teams against each other in music-trivia rounds built around pop culture rather than musical…
entries.text: The television series that pits two celebrity-captained teams against each other in music-trivia rounds built around pop culture rather than musical expertise, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast on BBC Two November 12, 1996, produced by Talkback. Its signature "Intros" round has one team member convey a song's introduction entirely a cappella for a teammate to identify, converting a purely instrumental piece of music into something one person has to perform vocally without singing an actual lyric.

entries.name: The Great Pottery Throw Down
entries.author: Love Productions
entries.awards: none — the format has drawn no major industry-award recognition of its own, despite coming from the same production company, Love Productions, behind The Great British Bake Off.
entries.description: The television series that has amateur potters build and decorate ceramic pieces against the clock before kiln firing, judged on both a substantial…
entries.text: The television series that has amateur potters build and decorate ceramic pieces against the clock before kiln firing, judged on both a substantial weekly "main make" and a smaller supplementary skills challenge, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast on BBC Two November 3, 2015, produced by Love Productions. Its own production company built the format directly on the competitive-elimination-baking template it had already established with The Great British Bake Off, applying the same structure to a craft where the failure point — a piece cracking or exploding in the kiln — can destroy hours of work invisibly, off camera, between one scene and the next.

entries.name: Family Feud
entries.author: Mark Goodson
entries.awards: Daytime Emmy for Outstanding Game/Audience Participation Show, 1977 and 2019; Daytime Emmy for Outstanding Game Show Host awarded to Richard Dawson in 1978 and to Steve Harvey in 2014, 2017, and 2022.
entries.description: The television series that has two families compete to match the most popular answers a survey of one hundred people gave to a given question, first…
entries.text: The television series that has two families compete to match the most popular answers a survey of one hundred people gave to a given question, first commissioned by ABC in the United States and first broadcast July 12, 1976, created by Mark Goodson. Its face-off round rewards speed over certainty — a contestant who buzzes in first with the survey's single most popular answer wins the face-off outright, even against a rival family holding a technically correct but less popular response still unspoken on the board.

entries.name: American Ninja Warrior
entries.author: developed for G4 by Neal Tiles, adapted from the Japanese format Sasuke
entries.awards: Producers Guild of America Award nomination, 2016, for Outstanding Producer of Competition Television.
entries.description: The television series that runs amateur and professional obstacle-course athletes through a tiered qualifier-to-finals structure culminating in a…
entries.text: The television series that runs amateur and professional obstacle-course athletes through a tiered qualifier-to-finals structure culminating in a four-stage course on the Las Vegas Strip, first commissioned by G4 in the United States and first broadcast December 12, 2009, adapted from the Japanese competition show Sasuke. Once producers Arthur Smith and Kent Weed took the format over starting in its second season, they built the American version's own multi-city qualifying structure and a domestic Las Vegas final in place of the original format's practice of sending competitors on to compete in Japan.

entries.name: Big Brother
entries.author: John de Mol Jr.
entries.awards: none — the original Dutch production drew no major international award recognition in its own right; the format's significance rests on how many territories adopted its structure rather than on a competitive-award record.
entries.description: The television series that isolates a group of strangers together in a single house under constant camera surveillance, eliminating one housemate at…
entries.text: The television series that isolates a group of strangers together in a single house under constant camera surveillance, eliminating one housemate at a time until a single winner remains, first commissioned by Veronica in the Netherlands and first broadcast September 16, 1999, created by John de Mol Jr. Producers found during the first season that the format worked better as continuous, near-unedited daily broadcasts than as a heavily produced weekly highlights show, a lesson that shaped how dozens of the format's international versions — including the US, UK, and German editions — schedule their own daily and weekly programming mix.

entries.name: The Voice of Holland
entries.author: John de Mol Jr. and Roel van Velzen
entries.awards: none — the original Dutch production drew no major international award recognition in its own right, unlike some of the more than seventy territorial versions the format later spawned.
entries.description: The television series that has coaches judge singers in blind auditions from chairs facing away from the stage, hearing voice alone before turning…
entries.text: The television series that has coaches judge singers in blind auditions from chairs facing away from the stage, hearing voice alone before turning around to claim a contestant for their own team, first commissioned by RTL 4 in the Netherlands and first broadcast September 17, 2010, created by John de Mol Jr. and Roel van Velzen. Its blind-audition mechanic, the format's defining structural idea, was built specifically to remove appearance from a judge's first decision — a corrective aimed directly at the visual-first casting habits of the singing-competition formats, Idol included, that came before it.

entries.name: Miljoenenjacht
entries.author: Endemol
entries.awards: none — the format's significance is measured by licensing reach, more than sixty territorial versions, rather than by any competitive industry award won under its original Dutch title or any international one.
entries.description: The television series that has a contestant choose one sealed case at the outset without opening it, then progressively eliminate the other cases…
entries.text: The television series that has a contestant choose one sealed case at the outset without opening it, then progressively eliminate the other cases while a "Banker" makes offers, calculated below the cases' true expected value, to buy the original choice back unopened, first commissioned in the Netherlands and first broadcast in November 2000, produced by Endemol. Its now-signature case game wasn't actually part of the show's original 2000 format at all — it was added in December 2002 after a fifteen-month hiatus, meaning the mechanic that more than sixty countries would eventually license under the title Deal or No Deal is younger than the show itself.

entries.name: La Casa de Papel
entries.author: Álex Pina
entries.awards: International Emmy Award for Best Drama Series, 2018, at the 46th International Emmy Awards.
entries.description: The television series that follows a mastermind's crew as they take hostages inside Spain's Royal Mint to print billions of euros rather than steal…
entries.text: The television series that follows a mastermind's crew as they take hostages inside Spain's Royal Mint to print billions of euros rather than steal money that already exists, first commissioned by Antena 3 in Spain and first broadcast May 2, 2017, created by Álex Pina. After a modest domestic run, Netflix's international rerelease under the English title Money Heist made it one of the platform's most-watched non-English-language titles worldwide, prompting an official scripted remake, Money Heist: Korea – Joint Economic Area (2022), that relocated the same heist structure to a reunified Korean peninsula with an entirely new cast.

entries.name: King of Mask Singer
entries.author: Wonwoo Park
entries.awards: none — the original Korean production drew no major international award recognition in its own right, despite becoming the source format for more than forty territorial versions.
entries.description: The television series that has singers perform fully masked and costumed so panelists judge voice alone, unmasking the loser at the end of each…
entries.text: The television series that has singers perform fully masked and costumed so panelists judge voice alone, unmasking the loser at the end of each round to reveal a hidden celebrity identity, first commissioned by Munhwa Broadcasting Corporation in South Korea and first broadcast February 18, 2015, created by Wonwoo Park. The Korean original runs each tournament to a conclusion within two weekly episodes, a pace most of its international versions — built instead around months-long seasonal formats — never adopted.

entries.name: Yo Soy Betty, la Fea
entries.author: Fernando Gaitán
entries.awards: none — the original Colombian production drew no major international award recognition in its own right; its significance rests on its later reputation as the first telenovela ever remade worldwide rather than on a competitive-award record.
entries.description: The television series that follows an unglamorous, highly capable executive assistant who is undervalued and mocked at the fashion company she…
entries.text: The television series that follows an unglamorous, highly capable executive assistant who is undervalued and mocked at the fashion company she quietly keeps running, first commissioned by RCN Televisión in Colombia and first broadcast October 25, 1999, created by Fernando Gaitán. Its central premise proved portable enough to be rewritten from scratch in dozens of countries rather than simply dubbed, including the American network adaptation Ugly Betty, making it one of this collection's clearest cases of a scripted format, not just a game-show template, traveling internationally through full local remakes.

entries.name: The Office (UK)
entries.author: Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant
entries.awards: British Comedy Award for Best New TV Comedy, 2001; Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Musical or Comedy, 2002; Peabody Award, 2003; Ricky Gervais won the Golden Globe for Best Actor in a Television Series Musical or Comedy in 2004.
entries.description: The television series that shot an ordinary paper-merchant office as a single-camera mockumentary with no laughter track, treating a mundane…
entries.text: The television series that shot an ordinary paper-merchant office as a single-camera mockumentary with no laughter track, treating a mundane workplace as if a real documentary crew were filming it, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast July 9, 2001, created by Ricky Gervais and Stephen Merchant. Its single-camera, unscored, faux-documentary style was unusual enough for British sitcoms at the time that its influence is traceable directly into later comedies built the same way, and its American remake on NBC became a Primetime Emmy winner in its own right, with Gervais and Merchant staying on as executive producers.

entries.name: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?
entries.author: David Briggs, Mike Whitehill, and Steven Knight
entries.awards: BAFTA Television Award for Best Entertainment Programme, 1999; seven National Television Awards for Most Popular Quiz Programme, 1999 through 2005; the American primetime edition won two Daytime Emmy Awards, and host Meredith Vieira won multiple Emmys for Outstanding Game Show Host.
entries.description: The television series that lets a single contestant climb a ladder of increasingly difficult multiple-choice questions toward a top cash prize,…
entries.text: The television series that lets a single contestant climb a ladder of increasingly difficult multiple-choice questions toward a top cash prize, protected at fixed "safety net" thresholds they cannot fall below once reached, first commissioned by ITV in the United Kingdom and first broadcast September 4, 1998, developed by David Briggs, Mike Whitehill, and Steven Knight. Licensed into roughly 100 countries, it is frequently cited as the best-selling television format in the medium's history, a claim built on breadth of adoption rather than on any single version's ratings or award record.

entries.name: Manē no Tora
entries.author: Nippon TV
entries.awards: none — the original Japanese production drew no major international award recognition in its own right; its most decorated descendant, the American Shark Tank, later won the Emmy for Outstanding Structured Reality Program twice, in 2014 and again in 2024.
entries.description: The television series that has entrepreneurs pitch business ideas to a panel of wealthy investors for on-air funding, walking away with nothing if…
entries.text: The television series that has entrepreneurs pitch business ideas to a panel of wealthy investors for on-air funding, walking away with nothing if they can't secure the pitch's stated minimum investment, first commissioned by Nippon TV in Japan and first broadcast in October 2001. Its British adaptation, Dragons' Den, launched in 2005 as the format's first international version and set the "dragons" terminology that shaped the American Shark Tank and dozens of further versions, most of which kept some predatory-animal name for their own panel of investors regardless of language.

entries.name: Takeshi's Castle
entries.author: Tokyo Broadcasting System
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry-award recognition under its original Japanese title, its international reach measured instead by the range of ways different territories chose to relicense and re-dub it.
entries.description: The television series that runs a large field of contestants through elimination-style physical challenges building toward a final assault on a…
entries.text: The television series that runs a large field of contestants through elimination-style physical challenges building toward a final assault on a fortified castle, first commissioned by Tokyo Broadcasting System in Japan and first broadcast October 19, 1986. Its most widely seen version outside Japan, the American redub Most Extreme Elimination Challenge, replaced the original Japanese dialogue and commentary entirely with unrelated comedic English narration rather than translating it, and Wipeout, drafted earlier in this collection's Non-Scripted Formats category, drew acknowledged inspiration from the same underlying Japanese physical-challenge lineage — a connection close enough that a copyright dispute followed.

entries.name: Wife Swap (UK original)
entries.author: Channel 4
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry-award recognition under its original British run.
entries.description: The television series that swaps a member of two households for two weeks, first requiring the visiting spouse to follow the original household's…
entries.text: The television series that swaps a member of two households for two weeks, first requiring the visiting spouse to follow the original household's existing rules before letting them impose new rules of their own in the second week, first commissioned by Channel 4 in the United Kingdom and first broadcast January 7, 2003. An earlier American pilot attempt wasn't picked up at all, and it took a second attempt before the format found its footing on ABC in 2004, where the US version went on to run six seasons and spin off Celebrity Wife Swap — a reminder that a format's first attempt at crossing into a new market doesn't always succeed.

entries.name: Come Dine with Me
entries.author: Channel 4
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry-award recognition under its original British run, its cultural reach eventually extending as far as a 2024 stage-musical adaptation that premiered at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe.
entries.description: The television series that has four or five amateur cooks living in the same area take turns hosting a three-course dinner party for the others, who…
entries.text: The television series that has four or five amateur cooks living in the same area take turns hosting a three-course dinner party for the others, who privately score each host on the taxi ride home before a winner is revealed, first commissioned by Channel 4 in the United Kingdom and first broadcast January 10, 2005. Its scoring structure — private, delivered after the fact, and collected from guests who are also each other's competitors — builds a specific kind of dramatic irony into the format, since the audience hears verdicts the host being judged never gets to hear delivered to their face.

entries.name: De Verraders
entries.author: Marc Pos and Jasper Hoogendoorn
entries.awards: none — the original Dutch production drew no major international award recognition in its own right, ahead of its UK and US remakes' own award runs.
entries.description: The television series that hides a small group of "traitors" among a larger group of "faithful" players, all competing for a shared prize the…
entries.text: The television series that hides a small group of "traitors" among a larger group of "faithful" players, all competing for a shared prize the traitors can secretly steal for themselves, unmasking suspects at a nightly round-table vote that only the faithful, not the audience, are kept blind to, first commissioned by RTL 4 in the Netherlands and first broadcast March 13, 2021, created by Marc Pos and Jasper Hoogendoorn. Its central asymmetry — the audience always knows who the traitors are, while the faithful players never do — is what makes the format work as television rather than as a pure game, since every faithful player's contribution the format actually broadcasts is watched by an audience already in on the secret the player is trying to work out.

entries.name: Gift ved første blik
entries.author: DR, Denmark
entries.awards: none — the original Danish production drew no major international award recognition in its own right.
entries.description: The television series that has relationship experts match strangers for a legally binding wedding before the couple has ever met, following them…
entries.text: The television series that has relationship experts match strangers for a legally binding wedding before the couple has ever met, following them through the following weeks as they decide whether to stay married, first commissioned by DR in Denmark and first broadcast in 2013. Its structural bet is that removing courtship entirely — no dating, no engagement, just an expert-matched ceremony on day one — makes the process of a relationship's early weeks, normally compressed or skipped in most television treatments of romance, the actual subject of the show rather than its backstory.

entries.name: The Great British Bake Off
entries.author: Anna Beattie, for Love Productions
entries.awards: BAFTA Television Award for Features, 2012, 2013, and 2016.
entries.description: The television series that has amateur bakers complete a signature bake, a technical challenge, and a show-stopper across each episode, judged for…
entries.text: The television series that has amateur bakers complete a signature bake, a technical challenge, and a show-stopper across each episode, judged for taste, technique, and presentation inside a bunting-decorated marquee built to recreate an English village fête, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast August 17, 2010, conceived by producer Anna Beattie at Love Productions after she learned about American state-fair baking contests. Licensed to 196 territories by 2015, its most direct American descendant, The Great American Baking Show, kept the same three-challenge structure and even retained judges Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood, making it one of this collection's rare remakes that exported its original panel along with its format.

entries.name: The X Factor
entries.author: Simon Cowell
entries.awards: none — the format itself drew no major British industry award in its own right; its scale is measured instead by reach, with over 50 territorial versions and 256 total winners across the franchise.
entries.description: The television series that judges singing contestants through auditions, "bootcamp," and live televised results shows building toward a public-vote…
entries.text: The television series that judges singing contestants through auditions, "bootcamp," and live televised results shows building toward a public-vote final, first commissioned by ITV in the United Kingdom and first broadcast September 4, 2004, created by Simon Cowell as Pop Idol's direct successor. Its title names the very thing the format claims it can identify but never defines — "the X factor," an undefinable star quality judges are asked to recognize on sight rather than measure by any stated criterion, built as the format's whole premise rather than as marketing language layered on afterward.

entries.name: The Weakest Link
entries.author: Fintan Coyle and Cathy Dunning
entries.awards: none — the format itself drew no major British industry award in its own right; industry accounts rank it the second most internationally licensed quiz franchise, behind only Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?
entries.description: The television series that has a team of contestants build a shared money chain through general-knowledge questions, then vote one teammate out as…
entries.text: The television series that has a team of contestants build a shared money chain through general-knowledge questions, then vote one teammate out as "the weakest link" at the end of every round regardless of how well that teammate actually answered, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast August 14, 2000, created by Fintan Coyle and Cathy Dunning. Its host Anne Robinson's deliberately cold, dismissive persona was as much a part of the original format as the money-chain mechanic itself, and later versions abroad — a 2002 American edition, then a 2020 NBC revival hosted by Jane Lynch — largely abandoned that disciplinarian tone rather than reproducing it.

entries.name: Expedition Robinson
entries.author: Charlie Parsons
entries.awards: none — the original Swedish production drew no major international award recognition in its own right, well before its American remake, Survivor, became one of the most Emmy-nominated formats of its genre.
entries.description: The television series that strands contestants on a remote island to compete in physical and social challenges, voting one participant off at a…
entries.text: The television series that strands contestants on a remote island to compete in physical and social challenges, voting one participant off at a "council" each episode, first commissioned by SVT in Sweden and first broadcast September 13, 1997, created by Charlie Parsons, who had developed the concept for the British production company Planet 24 three years earlier. Its first season was overshadowed by the death of an eliminated contestant days after filming, a tragedy that shaped how every subsequent version of the format, including the American Survivor drafted earlier in this collection's Non-Scripted Formats category, handles post-show contestant welfare.

entries.name: I Am a Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here!
entries.author: London Weekend Television
entries.awards: Sir Bruce Forsyth Entertainment Award, National Television Awards, 2022.
entries.description: The television series that drops celebrities into a jungle camp where public votes send them into "Bushtucker Trials" for food and rewards the whole…
entries.text: The television series that drops celebrities into a jungle camp where public votes send them into "Bushtucker Trials" for food and rewards the whole camp otherwise goes without, first commissioned by ITV in the United Kingdom and first broadcast August 25, 2002, created by London Weekend Television. Because camp food rations are tied directly to how well contestants perform in trials the public chooses for them, the audience vote functions as a genuine resource-allocation mechanic rather than a purely cosmetic popularity contest layered on top of an otherwise fixed game.

entries.name: American Gladiators
entries.author: Dann Carr and Johnny C. Ferraro
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry-award recognition under its original American run.
entries.description: The television series that pits ordinary athletic contestants against a roster of resident professional "Gladiators" across strength, speed, and…
entries.text: The television series that pits ordinary athletic contestants against a roster of resident professional "Gladiators" across strength, speed, and combat-style events, first commissioned in first-run syndication in the United States and first broadcast September 9, 1989, created by Dann Carr and Johnny C. Ferraro. Britain's ITV became the first country to license the format in 1992, under the shortened title Gladiators — the version most widely remembered internationally today, including in the BBC's own 2024 relaunch — which makes this American original the less-recognized half of a remake relationship many viewers outside the US assume runs in the opposite direction.

entries.name: Ready Steady Cook
entries.author: BBC
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry-award recognition under its original British run.
entries.description: The television series that gives two competing home cooks a fixed-budget bag of ingredients and twenty minutes to turn them into a finished dish,…
entries.text: The television series that gives two competing home cooks a fixed-budget bag of ingredients and twenty minutes to turn them into a finished dish, coached in real time by a professional chef, first commissioned by the BBC in the United Kingdom and first broadcast October 24, 1994. Its two teams are given color-coded identities, "red tomato" and "green pepper," fixed regardless of which cooks or chefs rotate through a given episode — a branding device built into the format itself rather than into any single episode's casting.

entries.name: Naked Attraction
entries.author: Studio Lambert
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry-award recognition under its original British run.
entries.description: The television series that has a single contestant choose a date by eliminating fully nude candidates one revealed body section at a time, from the…
entries.text: The television series that has a single contestant choose a date by eliminating fully nude candidates one revealed body section at a time, from the ground up, before any face is shown, first commissioned by Channel 4 in the United Kingdom and first broadcast July 25, 2016, produced by Studio Lambert. Its elimination order inverts the usual order of attraction almost every other dating format relies on, deferring facial appearance and personality to last and forcing the choosing contestant's early decisions to rest on criteria the format itself controls the sequence of, not the criteria a contestant would naturally lead with.

entries.name: The Wall
entries.author: Chris Hardwick, LeBron James, Maverick Carter, and Andrew Glassman
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry-award recognition of its own in its American run, its reach measured instead by licensing into markets including Spain, Brazil, Australia, Canada, Chile, and Colombia.
entries.description: The television series that has contestants answer trivia questions to influence which of two paths a ball drops down a giant vertical pinball-style…
entries.text: The television series that has contestants answer trivia questions to influence which of two paths a ball drops down a giant vertical pinball-style wall, its landing value added to or subtracted from the team's winnings depending on how their partner answered the same question in an isolated booth, first commissioned by NBC in the United States and first broadcast December 19, 2016, created by Chris Hardwick, LeBron James, Maverick Carter, and Andrew Glassman. Unlike most of this category's other entries, its format traveled outward from the United States rather than into it, making it one of the few American-originated game-show exports in this collection's remake chains rather than one of the many imports.

entries.name: Hell's Kitchen
entries.author: Gordon Ramsay
entries.awards: none — the format drew no major industry-award recognition under its original British run.
entries.description: The television series that puts aspiring chefs through a working professional kitchen under a famously harsh head chef, eliminating contestants by…
entries.text: The television series that puts aspiring chefs through a working professional kitchen under a famously harsh head chef, eliminating contestants by vote or by that chef's own judgment across the run, first commissioned by ITV in the United Kingdom and first broadcast May 23, 2004, developed by Gordon Ramsay. Its first British series aired live nightly for two weeks with eliminations decided by public vote, much like Big Brother's format at the time, while the American version that followed switched to pre-recorded weekly episodes with eliminations made by the head chef alone — trading the original's live-television unpredictability for tighter control over the show's own pacing.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Ultra Q
entries.author: Tsuburaya Productions
entries.awards: none — the original anthology series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right, its legacy resting on establishing the format the rest of the Ultra Series would build on.
entries.description: The television series that anthologized standalone strange-and-unusual mystery stories in the mold of The Twilight Zone before any giant hero…
entries.text: The television series that anthologized standalone strange-and-unusual mystery stories in the mold of The Twilight Zone before any giant hero appeared in the franchise at all, first commissioned by TBS in Japan and first broadcast January 2, 1966, produced by Tsuburaya Productions. It was only after audience surveys showed children responding most strongly to the giant-monster episodes that producers increased that content going forward, a mid-run pivot in response to measured audience reaction that shaped Ultraman, the giant-hero series that followed it later the same year and defined the franchise ever since.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: ウルトラマン / Ultraman (1966 tv)
entries.author: Eiji Tsuburaya
entries.awards: Guinness World Record for the television series with the most spin-off productions.
entries.description: The television series that has a Science Patrol officer merge with a giant alien to fight kaiju threatening Earth, first commissioned by TBS in…
entries.text: The television series that has a Science Patrol officer merge with a giant alien to fight kaiju threatening Earth, first commissioned by TBS in Japan and first broadcast July 17, 1966, created by Eiji Tsuburaya. It was the first Japanese television series to use a bidding system for commercial sponsorship rights, a financing innovation that let multiple sponsors share a single production and gave the format the sustained budget that let it outgrow its own predecessor, Ultra Q, into the multi-decade franchise it became.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: 仮面ライダー / Kamen Rider (1971 tv)
entries.author: Shotaro Ishinomori
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right, its impact measured in merchandising and cultural reach instead: 620 million branded snack bags, 3.8 million toy transformation belts, and 300,000 bicycles sold during its original run.
entries.description: The television series that has a kidnapped biker remade into a cyborg by a criminal organization turn against his own creators, transforming into an…
entries.text: The television series that has a kidnapped biker remade into a cyborg by a criminal organization turn against his own creators, transforming into an insect-motif hero by force of will, first commissioned by Mainichi Broadcasting System and NET in Japan and first broadcast April 3, 1971, created by Shotaro Ishinomori. Lead actor Hiroshi Fujioka was seriously injured in a motorcycle stunt early in production, forcing the show to rework its own filming schedule and lean more heavily on doubles and voice-only performance for a stretch of episodes — a real production accident that reshaped how the series was actually made partway through its own first run.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Kikaider
entries.author: Shotaro Ishinomori
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right.
entries.description: The television series that follows an android built with an unfinished "conscience circuit," leaving him only partially able to resist the…
entries.text: The television series that follows an android built with an unfinished "conscience circuit," leaving him only partially able to resist the villainous programming a rival scientist wants to activate in him, first commissioned by NET in Japan and first broadcast July 8, 1972, created by Shotaro Ishinomori. It was among the first tokusatsu superhero programs to add an end-of-episode safety notice warning young viewers not to imitate the stunts they had just watched, a broadcast-standards response to real incidents of children copying earlier superhero shows' action scenes.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: 秘密戦隊ゴレンジャー / Himitsu Sentai Gorenger
entries.author: Shotaro Ishinomori
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right, its significance resting on founding an entire ongoing metaseries rather than on any single competitive award.
entries.description: The television series that organizes a five-member color-coded hero team, each fighter's role and costume distinct from the others, against a shared…
entries.text: The television series that organizes a five-member color-coded hero team, each fighter's role and costume distinct from the others, against a shared criminal organization, first commissioned by NET in Japan and first broadcast April 5, 1975, created by Shotaro Ishinomori. It was the first entry in what became the Super Sentai metaseries, running new, unconnected team casts under a shared color-team structure every year since — a structural template every other Sentai title in this collection, including the one that would later become Mighty Morphin Power Rangers footage abroad, still follows.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Space Sheriff Gavan
entries.author: Toei Company
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right.
entries.description: The television series that follows a galactic police officer sent to Earth to fight an alien criminal syndicate, transforming into his silver Combat…
entries.text: The television series that follows a galactic police officer sent to Earth to fight an alien criminal syndicate, transforming into his silver Combat Suit through a command called "Electroplate," first commissioned by TV Asahi in Japan and first broadcast March 5, 1982, produced by Toei Company. It launched the Metal Hero Series, a second ongoing tokusatsu metaseries distinct from both Ultraman's kaiju lineage and the Super Sentai/Kamen Rider hero lineage, built specifically around lone officers and law-enforcement premises rather than color-coded teams or insect-motif cyborgs.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Choudenshi Bioman
entries.author: Toei Company
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right; a 2008 DVD reissue became the second-highest-selling tokusatsu release on that format, a commercial rather than a competitive-award distinction.
entries.description: The television series that gives five ordinary people superpowers drawn from "Bio Particles," and — for the first time in the Super Sentai franchise…
entries.text: The television series that gives five ordinary people superpowers drawn from "Bio Particles," and — for the first time in the Super Sentai franchise — casts two women among the five-member team, including its first female Yellow Ranger, first commissioned by TV Asahi in Japan and first broadcast February 4, 1984, produced by Toei Company. Producer Haim Saban built an unaired 1986 American pilot called Bio-Man directly from this footage years before Kyōryū Sentai Zyuranger became the actual Power Rangers source material, making this series the format's first, failed attempt at the American adaptation that would eventually succeed with a different Sentai entirely.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Kamen Rider Black
entries.author: Toei Company
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right.
entries.description: The television series that has a young man transformed into a cyborg hero forced to fight his own brainwashed stepbrother, who has been transformed…
entries.text: The television series that has a young man transformed into a cyborg hero forced to fight his own brainwashed stepbrother, who has been transformed into the story's chief antagonist by the same criminal organization, first commissioned by Mainichi Broadcasting System in Japan and first broadcast October 4, 1987, produced by Toei Company. Building an entire season's central conflict around two brothers on opposite sides gave the Kamen Rider format a serialized family drama it hadn't carried before, a structural shift toward ongoing psychological stakes rather than a new villain-of-the-week each episode.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Choujin Sentai Jetman
entries.author: Toei Company
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right.
entries.description: The television series that gives five bird-motif heroes powers drawn from a research device called the "Bio Bird System," built for the first time…
entries.text: The television series that gives five bird-motif heroes powers drawn from a research device called the "Bio Bird System," built for the first time in the Super Sentai franchise around a romantic love triangle and genuine tragedy among its own team members, first commissioned by TV Asahi in Japan and first broadcast February 15, 1991, produced by Toei Company. It was also the first Sentai series to have its team address each other by personal names on screen rather than by their color designations, a small script-level choice that marked a broader turn toward treating the team as characters first and a color-coded unit second.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Kyōryū Sentai Zyuranger
entries.author: Toei Company
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right; its American footage license became one of the most commercially significant such deals in the format's history.
entries.description: The television series that gives five dinosaur-themed warriors powers awakened after ten thousand years of suspended animation to fight a…
entries.text: The television series that gives five dinosaur-themed warriors powers awakened after ten thousand years of suspended animation to fight a resurrected evil sorceress, first commissioned by TV Asahi in Japan and first broadcast February 21, 1992, produced by Toei Company. Its fifty episodes of costume and fight footage were licensed wholesale into the first season of the American Mighty Morphin Power Rangers — including the Dragon Ranger costume, reused there as the Green Ranger — making it the direct footage source for the franchise that introduced Super Sentai's format to a mass American audience under an entirely different name.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Gridman the Hyper Agent
entries.author: Tsuburaya Productions
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right.
entries.description: The television series that has a teenage computer hacker merge with a heroic AI living inside his own computer to fight monster viruses from within…
entries.text: The television series that has a teenage computer hacker merge with a heroic AI living inside his own computer to fight monster viruses from within the machine, first commissioned by TBS in Japan and first broadcast April 3, 1993, produced by Tsuburaya Productions. It was Tsuburaya's first series to use D-2 digital video for its special-effects photography, a technical shift that allowed smoother slow-motion effects work than the studio's earlier analog-tape Ultra Series productions, and its 1994 American adaptation, Superhuman Samurai Syber-Squad, stayed close enough to the original footage and plot that it is frequently cited as one of the more faithful tokusatsu-to-American conversions of its era.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Ultraman Tiga
entries.author: Tsuburaya Productions
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right, its significance measured by popularity and franchise revival rather than by any competitive award.
entries.description: The television series that revived the Ultra Series after roughly fifteen years without a new television entry, set in a continuity deliberately…
entries.text: The television series that revived the Ultra Series after roughly fifteen years without a new television entry, set in a continuity deliberately disconnected from every earlier Ultra series rather than continuing any of their shared universe, first commissioned by Mainichi Broadcasting System in Japan and first broadcast September 7, 1996, produced by Tsuburaya Productions. It was the first Ultraman built around multiple switchable combat forms rather than a single fixed form, and released to mark the franchise's thirtieth anniversary, a revival successful enough that its title character reportedly received more screen exposure across television and film than any other Ultra hero from the era that followed it.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: 仮面ライダークウガ / Kamen Rider Kuuga
entries.author: Toei Company
entries.awards: none — the original series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right.
entries.description: The television series that revived Kamen Rider as a standalone television entry after the franchise had gone dormant on TV since Kamen Rider Black…
entries.text: The television series that revived Kamen Rider as a standalone television entry after the franchise had gone dormant on TV since Kamen Rider Black RX, rebuilding its hero around switchable combat forms in place of the earlier cyborg-transformation premise, first commissioned by TV Asahi in Japan and first broadcast January 30, 2000, produced by Toei Company. It was also the first Kamen Rider series broadcast in widescreen letterbox format, a production choice that, paired with its structural reset, marked it as the deliberate start of what the franchise itself calls its Heisei-era format.

entries.category: The Tokusatsu and Japanese Broadcast Line
entries.name: Kamen Rider Zero-One
entries.author: Toei Company
entries.awards: none — the series drew no major industry-award recognition in its own right.
entries.description: The television series that centers its hero's civilian identity as the CEO of a company that manufactures humanoid AI workers, building its…
entries.text: The television series that centers its hero's civilian identity as the CEO of a company that manufactures humanoid AI workers, building its season-long conflict around a three-way argument over whether humans and artificial "Humagear" should coexist, coexist under human control, or be exterminated, first commissioned by TV Asahi in Japan and first broadcast September 1, 2019, produced by Toei Company. As the thirtieth series in the Kamen Rider franchise and the first of the Reiwa imperial era, its own working title, "Rei-One" for "Reiwa's first Rider," was reworked into "Zero-One" specifically to double as a reference to the binary code its artificial-intelligence premise is built around.

entries.name: Black Mirror
entries.author: Charlie Brooker
entries.awards: Three consecutive Primetime Emmy Awards for Outstanding Television Movie, for "San Junipero," "USS Callister," and "Bandersnatch."
entries.description: The television series that anthologizes standalone, near-future stories about technology's darker turns, sharing no cast or setting from one episode…
entries.text: The television series that anthologizes standalone, near-future stories about technology's darker turns, sharing no cast or setting from one episode to the next, first commissioned by Channel 4 in the UK and first broadcast December 16, 2011, created by Charlie Brooker. Its move to Netflix beginning with its third series in 2016 gave the format a rare clean handoff between broadcasters without altering its identity, and its 2018 episode "Bandersnatch" pushed the anthology premise further still, using interactive branching choices so that no two viewings of the same episode necessarily played out the same way.

entries.name: True Detective
entries.author: Nic Pizzolatto
